title: Exhaustive case split on enum
summary: Prove injectivity of a rank function on an inductive status enum by exhaustive case analysis.
code: theorem statusRank_inj {s1 s2 : MemberStatus} (h : statusRank s1 = statusRank s2) : s1 = s2 := by
cases s1 <;> cases s2 <;> first | rfl | contradiction
triggers: prove injectivity or exhaustiveness over a finite inductive enum
combine <;> combinators with first | rfl | contradiction
prompts: Given a 3-variant MemberStatus enum and a rank function, prove two statuses with equal rank are equal.
Discharge all 9 pairs of a finite enum in one combinator line.
invariant: Finite inductive types reduce to a fixed grid of constructor pairs where mismatched ranks are contradictory.
mantra: Cartesian split with <;>, then close each cell with first | rfl | contradiction.
pitfalls: Using rfl alone fails on off-diagonal branches where constructors differ.
Forgetting contradiction leaves contradictory hypotheses like 0 = 1 open.

anchors.name: SWIM statusRank injectivity
anchors.trick: Chain cases s1 <;> cases s2 with first | rfl | contradiction.

mutations.explanation: Off-diagonal branches have unequal constructors and require contradiction.
